body: Business Standard 2023: rally mainly multiple rerating. Apr 2025 forward P/E ~2x historical (HAL 28x vs 14x; BEL 41x vs 21x). BSE PSU index ~5x Mar 2020–mid 2024 on capex ₹6→9.5 lakh cr.
title: Indian defence PSUs 2020–25: rerating, not earnings

body: The BSE PSU index rose ~5x from March 2020 to mid-2024 on government capex (~Rs 6 to ~9.5 lakh crore) and a narrative shift from 'value traps' to 'nation-building' stocks. Railway names (RVNL, IRFC) and defence/shipbuilding (Mazagon Dock, Cochin Shipyard, HAL, BEL) posted triple-digit gains; IRFC, a government lender, traded at a large multiple of book and RVNL, a contractor, at high P/Es (levels unverified). Business Standard (2023) found the rally was mainly multiple rerating; in Apr 2025 defence forward P/Es were ~2x their history (HAL ~28x vs ~14x; BEL ~41x vs ~21x). Peak: July 2024. Unwind: BSE CPSE index ~-30% from the July 2024 peak by end-Feb 2025; Mazagon Dock -59% and Cochin Shipyard -52% from July 2024; by late 2025 IRFC, Concor and RVNL were ~-46% and IRCTC ~-40%. The 4 June 2024 election result (no single-party majority) was an early crack (sharp one-day PSU fall, from memory). Defence had sharp rebounds in 2025 (geopolitics), railways briefly in Sept/Dec 2025. Top signals: valuations ~2x history with no matching earnings upgrade, heavy retail and thematic-fund ownership, government OFS selling into strength, high-stake PSUs (82-89% government) with tiny free floats. Lesson: rerating rallies end when multiples hit the ceiling, even when the capex story continues.
title: 2023-24 PSU, defence and railway rerating rally and its unwind
